scenarioStory.history: Patient reports sudden onset of severe, diffuse abdominal pain approximately 2 hours ago while at home, described as "the worst pain of my life." Pain has progressively worsened and is now constant. Denies vomiting blood or blood in stool. Reports feeling increasingly lightheaded over the last 20 minutes.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 55-year-old male lying on his side, pale and diaphoretic, guarding a rigid, diffusely tender abdomen. He is alert but in severe distress and reluctant to move. → Abdomen and shock assessed: Crew completes a focused assessment identifying findings consistent with a perforated or ischemic viscus, recognizes early shock, establishes IV access, and begins fluid resuscitation targeting a MAP of 65 mmHg. → Perfusion improves with fluids: The patient's perfusion improves following the fluid bolus. Crew provides advanced notification to the receiving hospital regarding a surgical abdomen with shock and transports rapidly with ongoing reassessment.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 55-year-old male lying on his side, pale and diaphoretic, guarding a rigid, diffusely tender abdomen. He is alert but in severe distress and reluctant to move.

scenarioEvents.name: Abdomen and shock assessed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes a focused assessment identifying findings consistent with a perforated or ischemic viscus, recognizes early shock, establishes IV access, and begins fluid resuscitation targeting a MAP of 65 mmHg.
relatedChecklist: Perform airway assessment and obtain full vital signs (pulse, BP, RR, neuro status)
Recognize rigid, distended, rebound-tender abdomen as signs of possible perforated/ischemic bowel
Assess for shock given hypotension and tachycardia; treat per Shock Guideline
Establish IV access; give 500 mL NS bolus pressure-infused <15 min (90 kg × up to 30 mL/kg = 2,700 mL goal; target MAP 65 mmHg)

scenarioEvents.name: Perfusion improves with fluids
scenarioEvents.description: The patient's perfusion improves following the fluid bolus. Crew provides advanced notification to the receiving hospital regarding a surgical abdomen with shock and transports rapidly with ongoing reassessment.
relatedChecklist: Provide advanced notification to receiving hospital: surgical abdomen with shock
Reassess vitals and abdominal exam en route; transport to appropriate surgical-capable facility

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid resuscitation delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Without timely IV access and fluid resuscitation, the patient progresses to decompensated shock with worsening hypotension, tachycardia, and altered mental status, now requiring repeat boluses and consideration of vasopressor support.
relatedChecklist: Recognize decompensated shock; repeat 500 mL NS bolus, prepare norepinephrine 4.5 mcg/min if fluid-refractory (90 kg × 0.05 mcg/kg/min starting dose)
